synopsis: The booklet presents adaptive stress testing (AST) as both an option for shortening validation and a failure-discovery method within the broader falsification and adversarial-search family [f425, f6936, f14148]. AST treats test selection as optimisation toward failures; the cited Stanford work uses dynamic programming and scene decomposition, and automated-driving simulations have demonstrated searches for the most likely failure trajectories [f6835, f634, f6838]. For this program, AST and reinforcement-learning adversaries are recommended primarily for sequential multi-agent failures, with academic toolkits and in-house tools identified as typical tooling [f7255, f7259]. Their results cannot establish failure rates unless re-weighted, and their effectiveness depends on the agent and environment model [f7257, f7258]. The cited independent evidence includes on-road and aviation applications; the supplied facts do not establish heavy off-road performance or quantify validation savings [f425, f634, f7260].
